author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correcting a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected: its date and description are shown for editing and can be changed under the booking's own validation rules. The correction replaces the values on that visit; the pet gains no second visit.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit is opened, then the visit form is shown carrying that visit's current date and description.
Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted to the same address, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown.
Given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet holds the same number of visits as before, and no additional visit is stored.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again with the submitted values.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again with the submitted values.
Given a visit that does not belong to the named pet, when its correction is requested, then the request is refused, as booking against a foreign pet is (Visits edge case 3).
Every behavior above is covered by tests.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit, or deleting one (NG-5 as narrowed 2026-08-28, and NG-4).
A link to the correction from the owner's record or any other page. The form is reached by its address alone this round; a visible entry point may follow as a separate request.
Moving a visit to a different pet or a different owner.
A confirmation message worded specifically for a correction. Only the redirect to the owner's record is required.
notes: NG-5 narrowed by docs/adr/2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-correction.md; the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR carries a status pointer to it. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md: (1) whether a visible entry point is added later, (2) whether the future-date rule should relax so a past visit's description can be corrected — narrowest reading applied, the rule holds, (3) whether a correction confirms itself to the reader — not required. Follow-up outside product-requirements-expert write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the 2026-08-28 ADR.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction reuses the aggregate-member edit pattern PetController already runs: an identity-aware @ModelAttribute loads the member through the root, form binding mutates it, and OwnerRepository.save cascades an UPDATE. The one adjustment is making VisitController's visit model attribute visitId-aware, so the booking path's fresh-Visit creation stops firing on the correction path. system-design.md Contracts now wires REQ-VIS-003 to Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController, and the invariant note records in-place editing of cascaded members.
integration_points: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit gains @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId; when present it returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and does NOT call pet.addVisit(...); when absent the booking path is unchanged.
Pet gains getVisit(Integer id) returning the visit with that id or null, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer).

Two new handlers on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit: GET returns "pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm", POST validates then calls this.owners.save(owner) and redirects to "redirect:/owners/{ownerId}".
The non-future-date rule is called from one private helper invoked by both POST handlers; no second copy of the rule is added.
docs/system-design.md Contracts Implements column and the Invariants paragraph under Contracts.
docs/adr/README.md index gained the 2026-08-28 row and marked the 2026-08-08 row as narrowed.

patterns.description: findPet: @ModelAttribute with an optional id path variable returning either a new instance or the existing member reached through the owner. The exact shape loadPetWithVisit must adopt for visitId.

updatePetDetails: an existing cascaded member is mutated in place and the root re-saved, never re-added. The correction reaches the same end state through binding rather than field copying, because the model attribute IS the loaded visit.
getPet(Integer): identity lookup over a cascaded collection, skipping unsaved members. Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors it.
The pet-not-found guard: IllegalArgumentException from the @ModelAttribute method. The visit-not-on-this-pet guard (Visits edge case 3) uses the same mechanism and message shape.

risks.risk: loadPetWithVisit is a @ModelAttribute method, so it runs before EVERY handler in VisitController, including the new edit handlers. Left unchanged it calls pet.addVisit(new Visit()) on the correction path too; owners.save(owner) then cascades that stray transient visit and the pet gains a second visit even though the edit handler never adds one. This is the slice's central hazard and it is invisible in the edit handler's own body.
risks.mitigation: Make the fresh-Visit creation conditional on visitId being null. The acceptance test theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddAnotherVisitToThePet must assert the pet's visit count after the POST, not just the redirect; with the mocked repository the test's own Owner instance is directly observable after mockMvc.perform.

risks.risk: Binding writes the submitted values onto the persisted Visit instance before validation runs, so a rejected correction leaves the in-memory visit carrying invalid values.
risks.mitigation: No write occurs. spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled and each repository call is its own transaction, so the Owner graph is detached; the error path returns the view without calling save. Do not add a save before the result.hasErrors() check.

risks.risk: Adding the non-future-date check as a second inline copy in the edit handler widens the controller-holds-business-rules deviation. architecture-principles.md line 91 states a new rule in a controller is a fresh violation not covered by the existing exception.
risks.mitigation: Extract one private helper in VisitController and call it from both POST handlers. This re-applies the existing rule rather than adding one. Moving the rule to a VisitValidator was considered and declined this round: @InitBinder setValidator would displace the @NotBlank description constraint that REQ-VIS-001's tests depend on, and addValidators wiring is scope this slice does not need.

risks.risk: Editing the Thymeleaf template risks two regressions. The submit button reads #{addVisit}; a correction-specific label needs a new key in all eleven bundles or I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails on partial translation, and the PRD names correction-specific wording a non-goal. The Previous Visits row carries th:if plus th:each on one element, where th:each binds first and the th:if filters the loop variable.
risks.mitigation: Change nothing in createOrUpdateVisitForm.html. The form has no th:action so it posts to the current URL, th:field="*{date}" and *{description} prefill from the model attribute, and visit['new'] already drops the New prefix from the heading for a persisted visit. The template satisfies the slice as written.

risks.risk: A visit id belonging to another pet, or to no pet, reaches the handler (Visits edge case 3).
risks.mitigation: Guard in loadPetWithVisit: pet.getVisit(visitId) returning null throws IllegalArgumentException with the same message shape as the existing pet-not-found guard. Refusal is by the same mechanism as edge case 1, which is what the acceptance criterion asks for.

notes: No ADR is written. The product decision is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-correction.md, and the mechanism is the existing aggregate-member edit pattern rather than a new one. Foundational check clear on all five signals. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization: the full owner -> pet -> visit chain is re-resolved per request in VisitController.loadPetWithVisit (owners.findById(ownerId), owner.getPet(petId), pet.getVisit(visitId)), each hop guarded by an IllegalArgumentException. A visitId belonging to another owner's pet is unreachable because the lookup never touches a visit repository - Pet.getVisit only scans that pet's own cascaded collection and skips unsaved members. No IDOR. This satisfies security-principles.md 'Trusting cross-request state': nothing is trusted from a prior request.

Mass assignment: the class-level @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") applies to both new handlers, so identity cannot be rebound. Visit carries only date and description and holds no back-reference to Pet or Owner, so the correction path cannot reparent a visit to another pet or owner. The @ModelAttribute Owner parameter binding on the POST handler is the pre-existing booking-path shape, adds no new field, and confers no privilege the already-open /owners/{id}/edit route does not.

Validation parity: the non-future-date rule was extracted into the single private helper rejectDateNotInFuture and is invoked by both processNewVisitForm and processVisitCorrectionForm, so there is exactly one copy of the rule. @Valid on the Visit parameter carries the same @NotBlank description constraint on both paths. No rule is weaker on the edit path.

Error handling: the new IllegalArgumentException message interpolates only the path-supplied visitId and petId, both bound as ints/Integer, so a non-numeric value fails type conversion before the message is built - no injection into the message. server.error.include-message is unset (Spring Boot default 'never'), so error.html renders an empty ${message}, and it uses th:text (escaped) with no stack-trace block. No internal detail, id, or credential crosses outward.

XSS: templates/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders visit.description and visit.date through th:text with Thymeleaf escaping on; no th:utext and no new unescaped sink. The form omits th:action and posts to the current URL, so no request-derived value composes a target.
Supply chain: no change to build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle.properties, or the wrapper - no new or upgraded dependency, so there is no new attack surface and no CVE delta to check.

Baseline note (not a defect per security-principles.md): the application has no authentication, authorization, or CSRF protection, and the two new routes - GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit - are open to every caller like every existing route. The owner -> pet -> visit object-level check is therefore the only thing constraining which visit a caller reaches, and it constrains reachability only, not identity: any caller can drive the corrected route for any owner. This is the documented demonstration baseline (system-design.md Security Context), and the change does not widen it - the new mutating endpoint mirrors the already-open visits/new POST.
